non_blocking_notes: Implementation assumes _SECRET pattern already defined in mission_control.py (referenced in project_saas_security validation but not shown in diff)
Lifecycle composition depends on the contracts of four composed functions (normalize, classify, bind, propose); any signature change would break run_saas_dry_run_lifecycle
result.reasoning_summary: The patch implements FW-SAAS-006 by composing four existing normalized stages (observation → finding → correlation → proposal) into a deterministic, auditable SaaSDryRunLifecycle class, then exposing it through a read-only SaaSSecurityMissionView projection in Mission Control. All acceptance criteria are satisfied: (1) stage ordering is preserved deterministically with event_id binding across all stages; (2) non-HIGH confidence findings fail before proposal output via existing validation in classify_saas_observation; (3) Mission Control view is a frozen dataclass with no execute/approve methods, explicit DEMO labeling support, and no callback authority; (4) comprehensive closed-fail validation rejects cross-tenant bindings, lifecycle tampering (kill_switch, deployment, authority flags), and secret-bearing content via pattern matching; (5) no provider APIs, credentials, mutations, or response executors are added. Test coverage is thorough: test_saas_integrated_lifecycle_preserves_stage_order_and_no_authority validates deterministic sequencing and audit trail; test_saas_integrated_lifecycle_fails_before_proposal_on_non_high_finding validates early-exit on invalid input; test_saas_security_projection_exposes_bound_lifecycle_without_authority validates read-only projection; test_saas_security_projection_labels_demo_and_rejects_tamper_or_cross_tenant validates all rejection cases. The code is pure, deterministic, and uses frozen dataclasses to prevent mutation. Scope is narrow and the patch adds zero external dependencies or capability paths beyond visibility.
